feedback: Iteration 0 has no race evidence, so this feedback rests on the contract physics and on what the controller had to do to work with this geometry. Sensing: with 12 mm sensors at 0.01 m pitch the readings overlap, and the signal is about offset/0.01 m, so kp of about 2 is a usable scale. The 0.06 m sensor lead should help the controller see the line early, but it adds phase lag, so kd was needed to damp it. If the next race shows steering_oscillation high or line losses on the slalom (a sign of lag), try reducing the sensor lead to y = 0.04 and keep the span. If the race shows line losses on the outer sensors at tight bends (readings saturating or dropping out near the tape edge), widen the span to x = +/-0.03 with a 0.012 m pitch or use a 0.016 m sensor. If the robot completes all three tracks with low oscillation but a time near 3 s, the drivetrain is the limit: try wheel_track 0.10 for quicker turning, or wheel_radius 0.035 for more ground speed per PWM. The off-track limit is 0.06 m for any body_width up to about 0.19 m, so body_width is not currently a constraint.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line losses or oscillation on the slalom, try sensor lead y = 0.04 (not 0.06) to cut phase lag; the 0.06 lead is the main unknown in iteration 0.
If the outer sensors read saturated or drop out at the tape edge on tight bends, try sensor span x = -0.03 to +0.03 with 0.01 pitch, or sensor_size 0.016, to extend the reach.
If completion_time is near 3 s with no line losses, try wheel_track 0.10 and wheel_radius 0.035 to increase turn rate and ground speed for the same PWM.
